business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Maternity and Infant Care Commodities

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Confederation of the Cantons; incorporation filed with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, e.g., Zug or Zurich)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary federal statutory system under the Swiss Code of Obligations, SR 220, with cantonal implementing ordinances)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1986, in force 1987)
Switzerland-China Double Taxation Agreement on Income and Capital (signed 2013, in force 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Arts. 305bis-305ter; Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 10 October 1997 (AMLA, SR 955.0), as amended; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Arts. 697j-697l (internal register of beneficial owners) and Arts. 621-629 (formation of the Aktiengesellschaft); Federal Act on the Implementation of International Tax Standards of 21 June 2013; Ordinance on the Commercial Register of 25 October 2023 (SR 221.411); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (SR 955.041.1); Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO sanctions measures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each natural-person shareholder, director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport/ID issuing authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) where the issuing state is a Contracting State; otherwise Consular Legalization through a Swiss Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and register of directors of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus certified translation into German, French or Italian if not issued in a Swiss official language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified criminal record clearance (Police Certificate) for foreign-resident UBOs and directors, if requested by the notary or bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization via the competent Swiss representation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation formalities executed abroad, if any
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss or foreign notary where the grantor signs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification and Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; certified translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original notarized deed of incorporation, Articles of Association (Statuts) and UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary in the canton of the registered office (e.g., Notariat Zug or Zurich)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial execution in Switzerland; no apostille or consular legalization required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against (i) the OFAC SDN list; (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) Swiss SECO embargo measures (SR 946.231) and the SECO list of sanctioned persons; (iv) the EU consolidated sanctions list; (v) the UK HMT consolidated list; and (vi) Interpol notices. Politically Exposed Persons are identified pursuant to AMLA Art. 4 and FINMA Circular 2020/1, triggering enhanced due diligence: source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, senior management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring. For a low-risk ISIC 4791 e-commerce structure, annual re-screening of existing UBOs and officers is the prevailing market standard.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX - Zentraler Firmenindex (www.zefix.ch), operated by the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI); incorporation filed with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) and published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Art. 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations and Art. 53 of the Ordinance on the Commercial Register (SR 221.411), the company name must be written in Latin characters; names drafted in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin script. The name must contain the legal form indicator appropriate to the official language of the articles: 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (German), 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' (French), or 'Società Anonima' or 'SA' (Italian). The name must be true, unambiguous and non-misleading, and must not infringe the protected interests of the Confederation, a canton, or third-party trademark rights.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written refusal from the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant may file a reconsideration request with the same office within 10 days of receipt. If the rejection is maintained, an administrative appeal must be lodged within 30 days with the competent cantonal civil court of the canton of the registered office. Final judicial review is available before the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) in Lausanne within 30 days of the cantonal appellate decision. The appellant must demonstrate that the name complies with Art. 950 CO and the Ordinance on the Commercial Register and that the refusal was based on incorrect legal application or manifest arbitrariness. Because Switzerland does not operate a statutory name-reservation system, a rejected name may be modified and immediately re-filed; no priority right attaches to an unreserved name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. Swiss law requires a real physical street address within the chosen municipality where the company can be served with process and official notices, as stated in Art. 626 CO. A registered office located at the premises of a licensed fiduciary, law firm or professional domiciliation provider is accepted in all cantons, including Zug. A purely virtual or letterbox-only office with no physical Swiss address and no authorized recipient for service of process is not permissible. For a low-risk ISIC 4791 maternity and baby e-commerce entity, licensed fiduciary domiciliation is market-standard and generally accepted by acquiring banks and payment processors such as Stripe and PayPal, subject to the provider being regulated and the address being listed on official correspondence and the company website.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 10% unannounced physical inspection probability per annum for a standard low-risk ISIC 4791 e-commerce AG maintaining a licensed fiduciary registered office; the probability materially exceeds 50% where the registered address is a pure virtual or letterbox address, or where UBO disclosure and commercial substance are deficient.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) incorporation publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille and consular legalization fee schedules of the issuing state

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss corporate-law counsel - pre-incorporation due diligence, drafting and review fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR/SR 220), Arts. 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft), notably Arts. 626–632 (incorporation), 640 (minimum capital) and 716a (board duties); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV/SR 221.411); Civil Code (SR 210).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Office; filings effected through EasyGov and published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung) together with the registration application (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) submitted to the Commercial Register through the notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum authorized share capital CHF 100,000; minimum paid-up capital CHF 50,000 (at least 20% of each share's par value) must be deposited in a blocked account (Sperrkonto) held with a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank; the bank issues an escrow-capital confirmation; free disposal of funds is permitted only after Commercial Register entry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Founders, having subscribed to the entire share capital of CHF 100,000 divided into 1,000 registered shares at CHF 100 each, hereby adopt the Articles of Association dated [Date] and confirm that the minimum paid-up capital has been deposited into the blocked account at [Bank]; that the registered office is established at [Address], Canton of Zug, Switzerland; that [Name] and [Name] are elected to the Board of Directors and [Name] is appointed Managing Officer with individual signature authority; that the Board shall apply for entry in the Commercial Register and declare the statutory-audit waiver permitted by Article 727a OR; and that the Board is authorised to execute all further filings and registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Adoption of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Beurkundungsstelle) of the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Deed of Incorporation, Articles of Association (Statuten), founder declarations and share-subscription statements; submit to the notary at least five working days before signing; all founders must attend notarization in person or through notarial proxy; the notary verifies identity, confirms capital subscription, and executes the public deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or Swiss ID of each founder
Confirmation of registered-office address and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises objections, amend the Statuten to conform with OR Arts. 626–628 and re-notarize; defective proxies must be re-executed or the founder must appear personally.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Verification of Paid-up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank maintaining the blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized deed to the bank; the bank opens a corporate-in-formation blocked account, performs KYC/AML verification of beneficial owners and source of funds, records the capital deposit of at least CHF 50,000, and issues a capital-deposit confirmation for use by the notary and Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Valid identification of founders and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a KYC query, provide the requested UBO and source-of-funds declarations promptly; if the escrow confirmation is delayed, escalate to the bank's middle office or select an alternate FINMA-licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Directors, Auditor Election and Audit Exemption Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders' constitutive meeting and, if required, a licensed statutory auditor (zugelassene Revisionsgesellschaft)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the constitutive meeting, adopt the first board resolution, appoint the directors and the managing officer, fix signature authority, and resolve on the audit regime: full statutory audit under OR Art. 727, limited audit under Art. 727a, or complete waiver for small companies; the auditor, if appointed, must sign an acceptance declaration.
required_dossiers: Auditor consent letter (if audit is not waived)
Statement on capital subscription and payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register refuses the audit-exemption declaration, retroactively appoint an auditor within statutory deadlines and file a supplementary resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug via EasyGov / notarial electronic submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration application electronically together with the notarized deed, bank capital confirmation, director consents, specimen signatures and registered-office consent; the Commercial Register verifies legal conformity, enters the company, and automatically assigns the UID business identification number.
required_dossiers: Consents and specimen signatures of directors and managing officers
Declaration concerning debts and over-indebtedness, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a formal deficiency notice, respond within the registry-set correction period; if omission is substantive, re-notarize amended clauses and file anew with the prescribed correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB) administered by the Federal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following Commercial Register entry, the registry automatically transmits the official notice to SHAB; the company verifies the published data (name, seat, purpose, share capital, directors and signatory powers); legal capacity to third parties arises as of registration.
required_dossiers: Automatic publication triggered by the Commercial Register entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB notice contains inaccuracies, file a corrective annotation with the Commercial Register within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal, Cantonal and Social Security Registrations (VAT, profit tax, AHV/AVS, accident insurance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for VAT; Cantonal Tax Administration of Zug; Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) for AHV/AVS; SUVA for accident insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the assigned UID; register for VAT within 90 days of formation if taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000; register for cantonal profit and capital taxes; register as employer with the AHV compensation office and SUVA; confirm warehouse waste and packaging compliance at the place of business.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is delayed, contact ESTV to obtain a correction and prospective registration; for social security, retroactive registration with the Ausgleichskasse should be completed within the same month to avoid administrative penalty interest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure online retail (ISIC 4791); product-safety oversight rests with the Swiss Federal Office for Public Health (BAG) and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for consumer goods and workplace conditions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license required; the activity is e-commerce distribution with office and low-impact warehousing only.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure e-commerce and general warehousing do not trigger an EIA category under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/EIAO).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge; sanitary wastewater discharged to municipal sewer conforming to the Federal Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV, SR 814.201); packaging waste from online-retail sales subject to the Waste Movement Ordinance (VeVA, SR 814.600); VOC thresholds only if cleaning or disinfecting products are stored, with applicable labelling and storage-state-of-the-art requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Cantonal Fire Safety Inspectorate for leased office and warehouse premises, including evacuation plans, extinguisher coverage and fire-load documentation; structural load and building compliance evidenced by the landlord's building permit; occupational health and workplace clearance under SUVA and SECO covering first-aid, ergonomics, electrical safety and staff safety instruction for office and warehouse operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), Value Added Tax Division, Bern; official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; electronic filing via the SIP taxpayer portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation the AG is automatically assigned a Swiss Business Identifier (UID) by the Commercial Register (Handelsregister). The AG must separately register as a VAT taxpayer with the ESTV through the online SIP portal using Form 'Registration as a VAT taxpayer'. Procedure: (1) submit company incorporation deed and certified Commercial Register extract; (2) designate Swiss domicile address and board representation; (3) if non-established abroad, appoint a Swiss fiscal domicile/representative for VAT; (4) ESTV issues the VAT number (MWST-Nr./UID) within approximately 3-5 weeks. Registration is mandatory once taxable turnover reaches the statutory threshold; late registration attracts procedural fines.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists; the AG is mandatorily taxed at entity level. Available elections: VAT group election (Organschaft, Art. 21 MWSTG); simplified budget method (Saldomethode) vs. net tax method; participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) election for qualifying capital gains and dividends; cantonal notional interest deduction (NID) elections under TRAF reforms; no domestic hybrid-mismatch election - BEPS/MLI measures apply through treaty provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax; MWST/TVA/IVA) - standard rate 8.1%, reduced rate 2.6% for qualifying baby formula/medical-type basic goods, accommodation rate 3.8%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover effective 1 January 2025 (formerly CHF 100,000); non-established foreign e-commerce suppliers crossing the threshold from Swiss consumer sales are registrable, while sub-threshold suppliers may opt for voluntary registration to claim input VAT recovery
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate in Switzerland. Swiss QR-bill (since 2020) is the preferred structured e-invoice format; PEPPOL/EBInterface exchange is used in B2B/B2G. VAT returns are filed electronically via the SIP portal or certified tax software on quarterly/semi-annual/annual cycles; no third-party clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% with input VAT credit) applies to goods physically exported from Switzerland, including cross-border e-commerce deliveries of maternity and infant care products to foreign consumers, provided the goods leave Swiss customs territory within 30 days of supply and proof of export is retained. Services directly connected to exported goods or performed wholly abroad are also zero-rated. Domestic online sales without genuine export documentation attract the standard 8.1% rate (or 2.6% reduced rate for qualifying baby food/medical supplies).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (e-dec / customs exit receipt)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR transport document evidencing physical departure from Switzerland
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank payment proof evidencing foreign buyer payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV audits export zero-rating claims and may retrospectively recharacterize the supply as domestic once export proof is insufficient; the withheld VAT (8.1%/2.6%) is clawed back with default interest of 4.5% p.a. Penalties: procedural fines up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 92 MWSTG); evasion surcharge up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 93 MWSTG); criminal prosecution for forged customs export documents under Swiss customs law (VStrR) with imprisonment up to 10 years in aggravated cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) – Schweizerische Nationalbank, in collaboration with the Federal Department of Finance and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland affords unrestricted convertibility for both current account and capital account operations. No exchange controls, surrender requirements, or prior authorizations apply to cross-border fund transfers. The regulatory framework is anchored in the Swiss Constitution's free movement of capital, the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments, and Switzerland's adherence to the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Profit remittance is permitted without foreign-exchange restriction; Swiss withholding tax (35% on dividends) applies but is subject to treaty relief. Only statistical thresholds under the Swiss Payment Statistics Ordinance require banks to report payments exceeding CHF 3 million in a month or CHF 250,000 for certain non-resident transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion regulations exist for export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency balances freely, settle trade debts in any currency, and repatriate funds without central-bank permission. Swiss money laundering reporting obligations require identification of beneficial owners for transactions above CHF 15,000 in monetary instruments, but treasury and corporate banking operations are not subject to any forced conversion regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Cross-border fintech EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex can serve as operational clearing rails for e-commerce disbursements only. They are not viable for capital escrow or treasury reserve purposes in Switzerland absent a Swiss FINMA fintech licence (Art. 1b Banking Act) or a full banking licence. These entities cannot legally hold client funds in segregated accounts for third-party treasury functions unless they maintain a Swiss branch with FINMA authorization. Their use is therefore restricted to secondary payment gateways, subject to bank-grade AML/KYC reviews by the primary Swiss relationship bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss banks generally permit complete remote onboarding for low-risk e-commerce corporations if the beneficial owners are natural persons and a certified video-identification process is used. However, the bank's compliance function retains discretion to mandate an in-person interview for director(s) at a bank branch or Swiss consulate. For non-resident-director structures without OECD tax nexus, most Tier 1 cantonal banks require at least one physical appearance by the authorised signatory or director. The act of establishing actual board authority through a notarised and apostilled board resolution is mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership complexity – multiple shareholders, bearer shares, or multi-jurisdictional ownership of the Swiss parent (CH_AG).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised extract from the Swiss Central Business Index (Zefix / SHAB), authenticated share register listing direct and indirect beneficial owners above 25%, a structogram showing the entire ownership chain, and a signed UBO declaration with passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds unable to prove clear economic origin for the initial capital contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12 months of audited or certified bank statements from the funding entity, tax clearance certificates for the source jurisdiction, a sworn affidavit on source of wealth, and audited financial statements for the CH_AG entity if already capitalised.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction link in the customer's trade counterparties or payment-rail partners (e.g., Stripe or PayPal processing for jurisdictions on FATF lists).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction flow analysis with counterparty due diligence, sanctions and PEP screening results, end-customer Risk Assessment Report, and a clear explanation of the e-commerce platform's jurisdictional coverage map with restricted-territory policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No demonstrable commercial substance or physical office address despite legal establishment as a Swiss AG.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement or shared-office agreement with a registered Swiss service provider, monthly utility or administrative invoices, photos/vidence of premises, and employment records of a local fiduciary officer if the company has no external staff.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity injections into CH_AG, the compliant routing is a SWIFT MT103 through a prime correspondent bank with explicit field 23B (Code: CRED), field 50K (originating beneficial owner), field 59 (beneficiary name and account at Swiss bank), and a purpose clause stating 'Capital Increase – Share Premium – Art. 632 CO'. Swiss banks require the submission of a capital increase attestation from the commercial register and the notarised bank confirmation of full subscription. For inbound capital transfers exceeding CHF 1 million, the Swiss National Bank's statistical reporting may be triggered, and the bank will require a short census form identifying the sender, beneficiary, and economic transaction code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement disbursements are executed primarily via SWIFT MT103 direct transfers or by documentary letter of credit (MT700), under UCP600. For low-value recurring supplier payments in Europe, SEPA Credit Transfer (everyday SEPA) is available because Switzerland participates as a non-EU SEPA member. For cross-border inventory procurement outside Europe, SWIFT MT103 with SWIFT GPI tracking is preferred, accompanied by commercial invoices and packing lists for bank-side value-chain verification. SWIFT non-repudiation and AML fast-track mechanisms apply, and all outbound trade payments above EUR 100,000 or CHF 100,000 trigger enhanced due-diligence checks on the underlying trade documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts for immediate settlement through the SIX Swiss Exchange or OTC counterparties.
Outright forward exchange contracts (non-deliverable and deliverable) with a licensed Swiss bank or regulated foreign bank under ISDA or Swiss Master Agreement for OTC derivatives.
Currency swaps (XCCY swaps) with authorised Swiss credit institutions, permitted for structural hedging of long-term foreign currency receivables.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) used in conjunction with floating-rate trade loans.
Vanilla European FX options (calls and puts) on major cleared currencies when documented as hedging, not speculative, transactions under FINMA market-conduct rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return package including signed annual accounts (Federal Direct Tax, Cantonal and Communal Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) forwarding to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) and municipal tax unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year AG: due between 31 March and 31 May of the following year depending on the canton; extension of up to 6 months generally available; annual filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 3.5%-4.5% p.a.; late-filing penalty up to CHF 10,000; default assessment by tax authority; administrative garnishment; criminal tax proceedings for wilful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) of shareholders approving the annual accounts and granting discharge to the Board of Directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book; no government filing required for a small AG exempted from statutory publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Held within 6 months after fiscal year end (30 June following a 31 December fiscal year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any shareholder may petition the court to convene the meeting; repeated failure constitutes a breach of corporate law exposing directors to personal liability; aggravated cases may lead to judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register (Handelsregister) data confirmation: annual register audit and event-driven amendments (directors, share capital, registered office, signatory powers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt), supervised by the Federal Register Unit (FRE-GEVER)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Switzerland applies event-based filing with no annual confirmation statement; a full register audit is recommended annually before the AGM; register changes must be filed within 7-30 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of up to CHF 5,000 for non-compliance with register orders; criminal penalties for knowingly false statements; refusal of subsequent registrations; adverse notation in the register excerpt

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Share register and Beneficial Owner Register (UBO) annual verification under OR 697j and the revised Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory registers kept at the registered office; made available to the statutory auditor, MROS and competent authorities upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation: any share transfer or change of beneficial owner recorded in the Aktienbuch and UBO register within 30 days of the company becoming aware; the Board of Directors must issue an annual confirmation statement before the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under AMLA of up to CHF 20,000 for negligent and CHF 100,000 for intentional breaches; suspension of shareholder rights in aggravated cases; blocking of dividend distributions if the register is found unlawful

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT (MWST/TVA) return - quarterly standard filing for e-commerce sales; reduced 2.6% rate applies to baby food and infant formula, standard 8.1% rate applies to non-food maternity and infant supplies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each calendar quarter for a standard e-commerce entity; annual filing permitted only when total taxable turnover is below CHF 500,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 3.5% p.a.; administrative fine up to CHF 100,000; tax evasion surcharge of up to three times the evaded tax; suspension of VAT refund entitlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage declaration (Lohnausweis) and social security (AHV/ALV/EO) wage statement for all employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse); wage certificate submitted to the cantonal tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Wage certificates must be provided to employees and filed with the Compensation Office by 31 January following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest of up to 5% p.a. on unpaid social security contributions; administrative fines up to CHF 30,000; recovery proceedings; loss of tax deductibility for the employer

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full statutory audit (ordentliche Revision) applies if the AG exceeds two of three thresholds in each of two consecutive years: total assets CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, 250 average full-time employees. If no full audit is required, a limited audit (eingeschränkte Revision) applies when the company has more than 10 full-time employees or a shareholder holding at least 10% of share capital requests it. An opting-out is permitted only when the AG has 10 or fewer full-time employees and all shareholders consent by unanimous resolution each fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR 957-959e) with Swiss GAAP FER in CHF; IFRS is permitted for entities not required to use it and mandatory for listed companies or regulated large groups; annual accounts comprise balance sheet, income statement and notes; cash flow statement is required only in specific statutorily defined cases.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Beneficial Owner Register (OR 697j) must identify every natural person who ultimately owns or controls at least 25% of the AG's capital or voting rights, or who controls the company by other means; each share transfer is recorded in the share ledger within 30 days; immediately before the AGM the Board of Directors must confirm the UBO register is current and accurate, refresh the AMLA disclosure and ensure the share register matches the Commercial Register excerpt.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO Register under OR 697j)
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board of Directors' Meetings
Share Transfer Record and Register of Capital Changes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 2,500 - 6,000 (USD 2,900 - 6,900) per annum for registered office, registered agent and corporate secretary services in Switzerland; additional CHF 60 - 120 per Commercial Register event amendment
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Limited audit: CHF 3,000 - 8,000 (USD 3,500 - 9,300); full statutory audit: CHF 10,000 - 25,000 (USD 11,500 - 28,900)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Swiss Federal Direct Corporate Income Tax: 8.5% charged on the after-tax (assessed) profit, equivalent to approximately 7.83% on the pre-tax base; in addition, each canton and commune levies corporate income tax, producing a combined effective headline rate for a commercial AG of approximately 11.9% (Canton of Zug) to approximately 21.1% (Canton of Zurich), depending on the registered seat and place of effective management.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays apply to online retail of maternity and infant supplies. Sustainable relief measures include: (i) participation exemption at federal and cantonal level for dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings (minimum 10% participation or CHF 1 million market value); (ii) notional interest deduction on surplus equity in several cantons including Zug; (iii) cantonal patent/innovation box exempting up to 90% of qualifying IP income; (iv) cantonal R&D super-deduction, e.g., additional 50% deduction in Zurich; (v) ordinary Swiss AG with real substance effectively pays between approximately 12% and 21% combined, and antiquated mixed/domiciliary company status regimes are being phased out under OECD Pillar Two.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official return: Cantonal corporate income tax return for legal persons ('Steuererklärung für juristische Personen') with integrated federal Direct Tax schedules of the canton of registered seat; lodgement through the cantonal tax administration e-filing portal or paper submission, with the federal tier administered through the same assessment file and reconciled with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one return per financial year; no quarterly return filing). Quarterly instalment payments based on the previous assessment are made on account during the year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed within six months of the financial year-end; for a calendar-year AG the statutory standard deadline is 30 June of the following year, and an extension to approximately 30 November is routinely granted on request; late settlement of instalments bears default interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Jahresgewinn (commercial book profit per Art. 57/58 DBG)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit shown in the approved financial statements (Handelsbilanzgewinn) after allocation to reserves but before federal, cantonal and communal income tax charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to the foreign shareholder; the taxable profit belongs to the Swiss AG as a resident legal person. Only a Swiss permanent establishment of a non-resident entity would report Swiss-source commercial profit in this box through its branch filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Aufrechnungen (tax recast add-backs, Art. 62 DBG)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory add-back of expenses lacking commercial justification: hidden profit distributions, excessive management or consultancy fees, non-arm's-length interest or royalties, and depreciation charges on assets not used for Swiss business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Crucial where the foreign parent receives disguised distributions; the add-back increases the Swiss taxable base and is simultaneously recharacterised as a dividend subject to the 35% Swiss withholding tax when paid or credited to the shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Beteiligungsabzüge und Reserven (participation exemption and deductible reserves)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from substantial participations and other legally recognised reserves; the participation exemption is granted if the shareholding is at least 10% or has a market value of at least CHF 1 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Completed solely by the Swiss AG. A foreign parent cannot claim the Swiss participation deduction on its own receipts; the AG must itself hold and document the qualifying participation before any group dividend is planned.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year losses against current-year taxable profit within the statutory maximum carryforward period of seven years; no carryback is permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss offset is a company-level attribute; the foreign shareholder cannot utilise the Swiss AG's losses against income earned outside Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Steuerbarer Reingewinn und Verrechnungssteuer (taxable net profit and withholding tax schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable net profit on which federal, cantonal and communal rates are applied; a supplementary schedule declares the 35% withholding tax due on actual and constructive distributions, bond interest and similar debt securities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG must withhold and remit the 35% to the ESTV within 30 days of the distribution date; a treaty refund application by the foreign recipient does not relieve the AG of its withholding and remittance obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a cantonal late-filing surcharge of approximately 6% to 10% of the assessed tax, plus default interest; a formal reminder then triggers discretionary assessment under Art. 130 DBG with a surcharge; procedural non-compliance carries fines under the Federal Administrative Criminal Law (VStrR) of up to CHF 10,000; intentional or negligent under-declaration additionally triggers the 'Nachsteuer' (shortfall tax) plus interest and a tax-evasion penalty between 33% and 300% of the evaded tax, with aggravated concealment escalating to criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) levied on the gross amount of cash dividends, stock dividends and constructive distributions made by the Swiss AG; capital gains realised by shareholders on disposal of the AG's shares are generally exempt from Swiss income tax for non-qualifying private shareholders under the treaty context.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss AG withholds and remits the 35% tax to the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) within 30 days of payment. The foreign parent resident in a treaty state files a refund application directly with ESTV using the official withholding tax refund form (ESTV Form 823 series applicable to the claimant's status), attaching: (i) a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority confirming residence and beneficial ownership, (ii) evidence of the dividend payment and of the 35% tax withheld, (iii) proof of the qualifying shareholding percentage and holding period, and (iv) a signed beneficial ownership declaration. Treaty relief typically reduces the rate to 0% to 5% for shareholdings of at least 10%; refund claims lapse three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid. Alternatively, a Swiss-resident parent may obtain an advance clearance/gross-payment authorisation from ESTV where the treaty exemption conditions are unambiguously met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss statutory withholding tax does NOT apply to royalties for IP, licence fees, or ordinary bank and intercompany loan interest; these payments may leave Switzerland without Swiss source withholding. The 35% withholding tax remains limited to interest on Swiss-issued bonds, notes and negotiable debt instruments, mortgage interest secured on Swiss real estate, and distributions on participation certificates, while treaty relief is correspondingly irrelevant for standard IP royalties and intercompany loan interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File, per OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines) must be prepared and maintained before the filing date where the annual volume of controlled cross-border transactions entered into by the Swiss AG exceeds CHF 2 million per tax year; Country-by-Country Reporting and notification obligations apply only to multinational groups whose consolidated group revenue is at least CHF 900 million (approximately EUR 750 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply ESR-style substance codes and has no general statutory anti-avoidance rule, but economic substance is constitutive for tax residence (registered seat and place of effective management per Art. 50 DBG), for treaty entitlement (beneficial ownership and the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test), for the participation exemption, and for avoidance of deemed-dividend withholding tax upon termination or relocation of the tax domicile. A Swiss AG without premises, staff, operational decision-making or commercially real inventory is exposed to classification as a domiciliary or shell company, denial of treaty relief, 35% withholding tax on the accumulated distributable reserves, and administrative strike-off by the commercial register authority. The Swiss Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax implements OECD Pillar Two for in-scope groups with consolidated revenue above the EUR 750 million threshold from 1 January 2024.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate or negligent omission of income from the corporate return, falsification of e-commerce revenue books, diversion of Stripe, PayPal or bank receipts to undisclosed accounts, systematic under-invoicing of maternity and infant goods sales, or destruction of accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the unpaid shortfall tax ('Nachsteuer') with default interest; a penalty equal to 33% to 100% of the evaded tax for ordinary negligence, rising to up to 300% for aggravated and systematic concealment; criminal prosecution under Art. 175 and Art. 186 DBG with fines up to CHF 1,000,000, publication of the conviction and confiscation of the evaded amounts; the discretionary assessment procedure under Art. 130 DBG adds a surcharge margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the de facto manager are jointly and severally liable to the tax authorities in civil recovery where they wilfully or negligently failed to maintain proper books and records (Art. 754, 957 and 958 CO); personal criminal prosecution for tax evasion and, where forged invoices or false certifications are used, tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG carries imprisonment of up to three years; investigative measures may include asset seizure and a travel ban against the directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Constructive dividends and transfer pricing deviations (hidden profit distribution)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length payments to a foreign parent or related party: overpriced purchase of inventory, management, consulting or IP licensing fees paid to an offshore group company without actual service provision, interest-free or low-interest shareholder loans, or abnormal rebate and settlement commissions lacking commercial justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment increasing Swiss taxable profit with default interest; the recast payment is recharacterised as a constructive dividend and the 35% withholding tax is assessed on the AG, which remains liable where it failed to withhold; treaty relief for the excess payment is denied, and stamp duty consequences may arise on deemed contributions; administrative fines follow Art. 62 DBG and ESTV transfer pricing practice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or caused the non-arm's-length contracts are jointly and severally liable to the company for the resulting tax damage and penalties (Art. 754 CO); civil restitution may be ordered against them for the excessive fees, and where the deviation is part of a criminal plan involving the Hong Kong-linked buyer or agent, directors may face prosecution for qualified tax evasion or money laundering with imprisonment and extradition-arrest risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and absence of economic substance (domiciliary company)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Swiss AG operating with only a registered address, no premises, no employees, no genuine operational control in Switzerland, no actual e-commerce inventory or fulfilment activity, and whose decision-making and commercial substance are located abroad with the sole purpose of obtaining Swiss treaty benefits and channelling profits to a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration disregards the company's Swiss residence, applies treaty abuse rules and the general anti-avoidance doctrine, denies the participation exemption, withdraws DTA gross-up and refunds, and imposes a deemed dividend on the accumulated distributable reserves at 35% upon termination or relocation of the tax domicile; the administrative dissolution procedure of the commercial register (Art. 164 ff. HRegV) may strike the company off the register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the entire 35% withholding tax on the deemed distribution plus interest and penalties (Art. 12 VStG and Art. 754 CO); where the shell structure is used for cross-border tax evasion or money laundering, directors face criminal complicity charges, seizure of personal assets and travel bans pending the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and unlicensed payment intermediary activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The e-commerce AG operating as a de facto payment processor by using its Stripe, PayPal or bank merchant accounts to collect and onward-remit funds of unrelated third-party merchants, or allowing the payment rails to be used for laundering criminal proceeds, without authorisation as a FinTech or payment institution under the Swiss Financial Institutions Act (FinIA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINMA enforcement action with discontinuation of operations, confiscation of unlawful profit, and criminal fines of up to CHF 500,000 under Art. 44 FinIA and the VStrR; conduct reaching the threshold of money laundering is prosecuted under Art. 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code with imprisonment, fines and confiscation of the laundered funds; the merchant accounts are frozen and the bank relationship terminated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permitted third parties to use the payment accounts are prosecuted as co-perpetrators of qualified money laundering and face imprisonment of up to three years, increased to five years for professional or band activity, together with disqualification from financial business activities; civil liability follows under Art. 754 CO for the resulting fines and sanctions, and the criminal authorities may impose international arrest warrants and travel bans against the responsible directors.
